subject: ophthalmology
title: Entropion, Ectropion and Ptosis

steps.tx: **Entropion** turns the lid margin inward so lashes abrade cornea, most often involutional in elderly lower lids from horizontal laxity, retractor dehiscence and orbicularis override, or cicatricial from conjunctival scarring diseases. Pain, watering and corneal ulcer risk follow lash touch. Temporary taping or botulinum buys time, definitive surgery corrects the anatomical components found.
steps.say: Inward margin turning gives lash abrasion of cornea in entropion disease. Laxity with retractor failure gives involutional mechanism in elderly. Surgery corrects anatomical components found.

vis.alt: Diagram of involutional lower lid entropion, showing horizontal lid laxity, disinserted lower lid retractors and preseptal orbicularis overriding upward.
vis.caption: Horizontal laxity, retractor disinsertion and preseptal orbicularis override are shown together turning the lower lid margin inward in involutional entropion. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Ectropion** turns margin outward, exposing conjunctiva and punctum so tears overflow despite watering eye anatomy being patent, involutional laxity again dominating elderly lower lids. Paralytic ectropion follows facial palsy, cicatricial follows skin shortage, each mechanism dictating tightening, graft or palsy care respectively. Punctal eversion alone explains epiphora with patent syringing, a favourite examination trap.
steps.say: Outward turning gives exposure with punctal eversion and tear overflow clinically. Patent drainage with watering gives punctal malposition explanation. Mechanism dictates surgical correction type.

steps.tx: **Ptosis** droops the upper lid from levator aponeurosis dehiscence in elderly, congenital levator dysgenesis, third nerve or sympathetic failure, or mechanical mass effect. Margin reflex distance and levator function measurements grade severity and choose operation: good function shortens levator, poor function suspends lid to frontalis. Pupil and motility examination must precede ptosis labelling because nerve palsies hide behind droop.
steps.say: Upper lid droop gives ptosis from aponeurosis, muscle, nerve or mass causes. Levator function gives operation selection between shortening and suspension. Pupil examination precedes labelling always.

steps.tx: The ruler in this picture turns a droopy lid into a number that selects an operation. **Levator function** is measured as the excursion of the upper lid margin from downgaze to upgaze while the thumb blocks the frontalis muscle, so forehead effort cannot inflate the result. Good excursion favours levator surgery, poor excursion points toward frontalis suspension. Letting the frontalis help is the commonest measurement error, which is why the immobilising thumb matters as much as the ruler.
steps.say: Levator function is the lid excursion from down to upgaze with frontalis blocked by a thumb. The number selects between levator surgery and frontalis suspension.

vis.alt: Clinical diagram of levator palpebrae superioris function measured with a millimetre ruler while the frontalis muscle is immobilised.
vis.caption: A ruler measures upper lid excursion between downgaze and upgaze while a thumb immobilises the frontalis muscle. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Levator function** measures upper lid excursion from downgaze to upgaze with frontalis blocked, normal about fifteen millimetres, poor below four guiding frontalis sling choice. Marcus Gunn jaw winking synkinesis raises lid with chewing from trigeminal levator miswiring, noticed feeding in infants. Function numbers, not photographs alone, therefore write the ptosis operation plan.
steps.say: Excursion measurement gives levator function grading for surgical selection in ptosis accurately and reproducibly. Poor function gives frontalis suspension choice in operation planning for children. Jaw winking gives synkinesis clue in feeding infants.

steps.tx: **Marcus Gunn jaw winking** needs severity grading because mild wink observes while severe wink with ptosis may need levator disinsertion and bilateral suspension for symmetry. Congenital ptosis with poor function risks amblyopia when pupil covers, urgency following visual threat not cosmetic age preference. Frontalis suspension materials and brow drive teaching complete congenital planning.
steps.say: Wink severity gives observation versus suspension decision in congenital cases together. Pupil coverage gives amblyopia urgency in childhood ptosis. Symmetry planning gives bilateral consideration.

steps.tx: Involutional entropion surgery combines horizontal tightening with retractor reattachment and orbicularis management, everting sutures temporising in unfit patients. Cicatricial entropion instead lengthens posterior lamella by graft after scar release, tightening alone worsening it. **Lamella logic**, anterior skin muscle versus posterior tarsoconjunctiva, decides which operation lengthens or shortens which layer.
steps.say: Component surgery gives involutional correction by tightening together with retractor reattachment in elderly lids. Cicatricial disease needs posterior lengthening by graft instead of tightening alone. Lamella logic therefore gives operation design in surgery.

steps.tx: Myasthenic ptosis fluctuates, fatigues and improves with ice or rest, with diplopia and bulbar features directing neurology referral rather than lid surgery first. Ice test improvement supports myasthenia at bedside before antibodies and electrophysiology. **Fatigability** history separates neuromuscular droop from static aponeurotic droop in one question set.
steps.say: Fluctuating fatigable droop gives myasthenia pattern needing neurology assessment first in clinic always. Ice test improvement gives bedside support before laboratory antibody tests return. Lid surgery follows disease control later in care.

steps.tx: Anchors organise malposition teaching: inward lashes abrade cornea, outward punctum overflows tears, and droop grades by levator function numbers. Mechanisms involutional, cicatricial, paralytic and mechanical repeat across all three malpositions in elderly and scarred lids. **Function numbers** choose operations while companion pupil and fatigue signs choose referrals before any lid is cut in theatre.
steps.say: Margin direction together gives entropion versus ectropion separation at examination simply and reliably. Function grading gives ptosis operation selection in surgical planning always. Companion signs give referral priority before surgery.

cards.b: Horizontal laxity, retractor dehiscence and orbicularis override; surgery corrects components together.
Good function shortens levator; poor function under four millimetres needs frontalis suspension.
Punctal eversion causes epiphora despite patent syringing.

keys: Cicatricial entropion lengthens, never just tightens
